models.when: DEFAULT arm — carries the most usage headroom on this host, so spend the bulk of ALL work here (implementations, research, docs, reviews). A different vendor from the qwen arms, which is what makes cross-vendor review possible. Its one cost is latency: prefill grows with context (roughly 36k→5s, 108k→26s, 306k→90s), so keep at most TWO agnes dispatches in flight, hand it self-contained briefs (say what to read and what to produce), and never pile a wide parallel fan-out onto it

the fast, scarce arm — use only when latency is the point (quick explore/search, log or file reads, a short answer someone is waiting on), to escape a stalled agnes arm, as the second-opinion vendor on agnes work, or for small/simple diffs; do not spend it on bulk work agnes can carry
the deep arm — multi-file refactors and hard debugging that need real reasoning depth or >512K context, and the independent reviewer of agnes-authored work when a qwen-vendor second opinion is wanted

workers.availabilityNote: Claude entitlement is routinely exhausted on this host; this arm is opt-in. Set "available": true to route here again — the brain still retires it for the rest of the run on the first failure of any kind.

models.when: heavier multi-file reasoning and a second review vendor. This host's Claude entitlement is spend-limited and routinely exhausted, so dispatch it only when the human asks for Claude Code, a change genuinely wants Claude-quality reasoning, or pi failed the same task twice — and retire it for the rest of the run on the FIRST failure of any kind (usage limit, auth, 5xx, transport, silent hang)
